Dancing in the Rain춤을 춰요

“Dancing in the Rain” asks for a hand to hold as the ground collapses. Its Korean title, 춤을 춰요, is an invitation to dance, placing an ordinary gesture of companionship amid destruction.

BACKGROUND

A little background

CJ Cultural Foundation’s introduction says vocalist Jang Kyungmin wrote the song while imagining the world collapsing and people dancing together as it disappeared. It appeared on Hello, Wonderland - EP, released on November 19, 2020.

INSIDE THE LYRICS

Holding on as the ground gives way

  • Companionship
  • Trust
  • Destruction

The speaker finds people difficult to trust but remains willing to love. That willingness first appears in an awkward, ordinary scene: drunken dancing and belongings falling from pockets. The request to take a hand makes closeness possible within that clumsiness.

As the images turn to collapsing ground, cuts and blood, the invitation to dance persists. The speaker’s assurances of being all right sit beside a request for companionship in the present; the danger remains. The closing embrace and movement into a dream can be read as a shared retreat from destruction, though the lyric leaves the pair’s fate unresolved.

ABOUT THE ARTIST / 라쿠나

Lacuna

Lacuna use imagined worlds and fairy-tale storytelling to write about lonely people and outsiders. Their name comes from the memory-erasing company in Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind.

The band began releasing music in December 2018 with the EP Incompleteness Dream. In 2019, they contributed to Mint Paper’s bright #8 compilation and performed at Grand Mint Festival.
